answer: Each seat needs its own network vantage: a plume of traffic that must rise from a distinct autonomous system and answer a challenge only that route can reach. Two seats behind one system share a vantage, so the later one is refused and a farmer must rent k separate transit paths from k separate operators. Clean, low-abuse systems are a finite orchard of rows; as they fill, the marginal vantage costs more than the last. A jade beacon rotated each epoch re-challenges every route, exposing resold or relayed paths, while honest agents simply renew the vantage they already hold.
